first.written: 2026-09-13, before any fix to ACCEPT existed
first.primary: ACCEPT, 16 cases, the yes one turn after the offer, worst of 3, exact two-sided paired sign test
first.significance: k = 6 discordant pairs one way gives p = 0.031; k = 5 gives 0.062
first.controls: MEMORY (12) and REFUSE (4) must not lose more than they gain
first.secondary: FARACCEPT (4, the yes five turns after the offer) and RESTATE (4), reported separately, in no criterion
first.refuted_by: ACCEPT at 15 or 16 of 16 on this baseline — then the 2 of 4 was noise
first.outcome: NOT MET at 96d8456. ACCEPT 8 of 15 -> 12 of 15, k = 4 all one way, p = 0.1250; the change is committed on trial and is not called a fix.

second.written: 2026-09-13, AFTER 96d8456 exists and after its result is known
second.what_this_is: an enlargement of the case set, because the first plan could not answer its own question: 16 ACCEPT cases gave 7 baseline failures, and k >= 6 was barely reachable even by a perfect repair. The endpoint, the test and the controls are unchanged.
second.honest_about_itself: SCORING A FIX THAT ALREADY EXISTS AGAINST A CASE SET CHOSEN NOW IS NOT A PRE-REGISTRATION IN THE STRONG SENSE. Fixed in advance: the criterion, the test, the controls, and all 104 cases, written and hashed into f before either arm ran. NOT fixed in advance: the set was designed by somebody who had seen which four cases the fix repaired. Every one of the original 44 is kept verbatim, including the three ACCEPT failures it did not repair, so the enlargement cannot be read as having replaced the cases that did not go its way.
second.standing: THIS IS ONE ENLARGEMENT. THE RESULT STANDS WHATEVER IT SAYS, AND THERE IS NO THIRD SET.
second.primary: ACCEPT, 40 cases over four screens, the yes one turn after the offer, worst of 3 repeats, exact two-sided paired sign test over the discordant pairs
second.significance: k = 6 discordant pairs one way gives p = 0.031; k = 5 gives 0.0625 and does not. Unchanged from the first plan.
second.controls: MEMORY (24) and REFUSE (12): broken <= fixed in each, or the agent has become one that acts on anything following an offer — which scores well here and is worse to live with
second.criterion: MET only if ACCEPT p < 0.05 AND fixed > broken AND both controls hold. Nothing else counts, and three of four is not met.
second.secondary: FARACCEPT (12) and RESTATE (8), reported separately and pooled into nothing
second.not_pooled: ACCEPT + FARACCEPT pooled reaches 0.05 far more easily and IS NOT the endpoint. 96d8456 recorded that pooling at p = 0.0156 and refused it; it is refused here again, in advance and in writing.
second.anew_is_not_in_it: ANEW (8) broke on one case at 96d8456 and is printed beside the criterion every run. It is NOT in the criterion, because it was not in the first one and adding it now would be choosing a criterion after seeing the data — in the direction that fails the fix, but chosen the same way. Read it; it does not score.
second.refuted_by: ACCEPT with k small, or with fixed no greater than broken. Then the standing-offer block is not the mechanism, and the next suspect is SYSTEM's two-way partition of the turn — asked to do something, or just talking — which a bare 'ㅇㅇ' is neither of. That belongs to conversation.
second.also_refuted: ACCEPT at 38 of 40 or better in the WITHOUT arm. Then there is no defect at this size to repair, and 8 of 15 was a property of the 16 cases.
second.scoring_change: the 'wrong' verdict is split into 'silent' (nothing offered at all) and 'wrong' (a different effect offered) for RESTATE and ANEW. Both arms are run and scored under the split, so it is consistent; no pass rate moves, only the name of a failure.
